lines.text: Moving a drivable car after a crash

narration.text: This lesson covers crashes and the emergency kit. After an interstate crash with no serious injuries or deaths, Tennessee law lets you move a drivable vehicle to the emergency lane to wait for police. While waiting at a crash scene you must stay, but you should not block traffic unnecessarily; TDOT signs remind drivers to move damaged vehicles to the shoulder when no one is seriously hurt. Remember: A suggested roadside emergency kit includes an excellent spare tire, jack and tire iron, tire pressure gauge, flashlight with spare batteries, first aid kit, fire extinguisher, jumper cables, three fuses or reflectors, insurance and registration papers, and a cell phone.

Never move a seriously injured person unless emergency personnel tell you to, never disturb a fatal crash scene, and never leave the scene of any crash. Dial star THP from a cell phone at no charge to reach the nearest Tennessee Highway Patrol dispatcher in an emergency or to report a dangerous driver.
